query: Consider the following context: Constituent phases and their corresponding phase transformations are important in developing alloys. In that context, which method can be used for control of phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The method of composition design and control of cooling rates can be used for control of phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni High-Entropy Alloys (HEAs), as it influences the formation and stability of constituent phases.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEA with a disordered face-centered cubic (FCC) solid solution phase
generation.intervention: Control of cooling rates during solidification, with a key parameter of cooling rate range from 10 K/s to 100 K/s
generation.conditions: Under atmospheric pressure and without external stress
generation.structural_mediator: The formation and distribution of coherent precipitates, such as L1₂ (Co,Fe)-rich nanoparticles
generation.mechanism: The cooling rate affects the nucleation and growth of precipitates, influencing the phase transformation kinetics and resulting microstructure [no specific record ID to cite]
generation.predicted_outcome: A 20% increase in the volume fraction of the L1₂ precipitates, relative to a baseline of slow-cooled (1 K/s) Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEA, with a corresponding improvement in yield strength by 150 MPa
generation.baseline: Slow-cooled (1 K/s) Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEA with a yield strength of 800 MPa
generation.boundary: Cooling rates below 1 K/s or above 1000 K/s may lead to undesirable microstructures
generation.uncertainty: The actual outcome may vary depending on the specific composition and processing history of the alloy, as well as potential interactions between multiple phases

falsification_experiment.design: Systematic variation of cooling rates and characterization of microstructure and mechanical properties
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured volume fraction of L1₂ precipitates is less than 10% or the yield strength improvement is less than 50 MPa, relative to the baseline, then the hypothesis is falsified
